title: More forgotten sessions: Howard McGhee, Goodman, Kay Starr and Lester Young
summary: Looking at discographies, Callender lists Los Angeles records of the Forties and Fifties he had not mentioned.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: We've been spending some time with some discographies, and you have discovered a lot of records that you forgot to name.

Yes. For instance, I just happened to be looking at a record with Howard McGhee on Black-and-White, called "Ood-I-Koo Bop." I didn't remember that. And another thing with Benny Goodman. I had forgotten I had done a record with him, "The World Is Waiting For the Sunrise." I didn't mention all that.

I'm looking at that here. Then Kay Starr, I did many things with her, including "Sweet Lorraine," "Melancholy Baby," "Sweet Georgia Brown." And there was a Hollywood Hustlers(?) with the Lamplighter, Ted Yerkes(?). Do you remember him? That's another one we used to record every night we got to work, we'd
I don't know the name of the studio, but we'd record every day. That was with Kay Starr; that was before she became a big name.
I see another record here with Sonny Greer, "Mood Indigo," "The Mooche"; with Lester Young, "You're Driving Me Crazy" and "The New Lester Leaps In" and the "D.B. Blues", "Lester Blows Again"...
All these were done in Los Angeles?
All these were done in Los Angeles. Red Norvo...
In the Forties and Fifties. But most of these, I would say, were in the Forties. Babe Russin, "All the Things You Are", "Like Someone In Love." And Andre Previn.
